b1-unit-02.02.1 Danny calls his mom:
Narrator: It's Danny's second week in São Paulo. He's on a video call with his mom, Rita.
Rita: So, tell me everything! Have you made any friends?
Danny: Yes, a few. Ana has been amazing. She showed me around Paulista Avenue on Sunday and invited me to dinner with her family.
Rita: That's so thoughtful of her. What's she like?
Danny: She's really cheerful and generous. She's a bit impatient in traffic, though! She tends to honk a lot.
Rita: Ha! Most drivers do. And what about the people at the hostel?
Danny: Well, I share a room with a guy from Porto Alegre called Bruno. He's very outgoing and funny. He knows everyone in the hostel.
Rita: He sounds nice.
Danny: He is, but he's not very tidy. His clothes are always all over the floor. And he can be a bit moody in the morning.
Rita: Ha! You're not very tidy either!
Danny: True! And then there's Mrs. Lima, the hostel owner. She seems a bit cold at first, but deep down she's really kind. When I was sick last week, she made me soup.
Rita: You were sick? Why didn't you tell me?
Danny: Mom, it was just a cold! Don't worry. I'm fine.
Rita: I always worry. That's my job. Are you feeling homesick?
Danny: Sometimes. I miss your pancakes. But honestly, I'm really happy here.
Rita: I'm so proud of you. Call me on Sunday, OK?
